title: The Greenland Shark Has the Creepiest Eye Parasite Alive
alt_titles: Why the Greenland Shark Is the Creepiest Fish Alive
The Greenland Shark Is the Creepiest Teenager in the Ocean
The Scariest Thing About the Greenland Shark Is Its Age
Why the Creepiest Shark Takes About 150 Years to Grow Up
thumbnail_brief: An extreme close-up of the Greenland shark's dot eye under the sea ice with the pale cartoon copepod streamer hanging off it (no eye damage), and tiny Doug in his cap with a torch waving at the copepod, which waves back, as the shark starts to turn, so the title's 'creepiest eye parasite' gets its twist from the text HI FRIEND? (never PARASITE, EYE, SHARK, GREENLAND or CREEPY; no bite, no attack implied).
description:
The Greenland shark is the longest-living vertebrate known: scientists dated the biggest one at about 392 years old, give or take 120, so some of the sharks under the Arctic ice right now are likely older than the United States. Doug meets Greenland sharks at every stage of that life, from a newborn pup to the oldest one ever dated, with a parasite on its eye, a top speed slower than a walk and a birthday cake.

Where should we send Doug next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe. Doug's death counter goes up faster than any shark's age.
